Dear Valued Investor,
We are pleased to provide you with the investor report for Blue Owl Real Estate Fund VI (“OREF VI”, “Fund VI” or the “Fund”) for the quarter ended March 31, 2026.
blocks.text: We are pleased to provide you with the investor report for Blue Owl Real Estate Fund VI (“OREF VI”, “Fund VI” or the “Fund”) for the quarter ended March 31, 2026.

blocks.html: Financial markets retreated in the first quarter following a strong 2025, as the conflict in Iran triggered an oil supply shock that pushed global energy prices higher. The S&P 500 declined 4.4% over the period. Equities had continued their upward momentum through January and February before pulling back as tensions with Iran intensified.2

blocks.html: With $315.0 billion in assets under management and over 1,390 experienced professionals globally as of March 31, 2026, Blue Owl invests across three multistrategy platforms: Credit, Real Assets, and GP Strategic Capital. Anchored by a strong permanent capital base, we provide businesses with private capital solutions to drive long-term growth and offer institutional investors, individual investors, and insurance companies differentiated alternative investment opportunities that aim to deliver strong performance, risk-adjusted returns, and capital preservation.

blocks.html: The Federal Reserve left monetary policy unchanged during the quarter, maintaining the federal funds rate at 3.75%. Chair Jerome Powell signaled that the pause reflected the Fed’s view of steady economic growth alongside inflation that remained somewhat elevated. Powell’s term concludes in May, and President Trump has nominated Kevin Warsh to take over the role.2

blocks.html: Fixed income was down during the quarter, decreasing 0.05% as measured by the U.S. Bloomberg Aggregate Index. blocks.html: Cap rates in the single-tenant net-lease market edged down slightly in Q1 2026, with the overall average decreasing by three-basis points to 6.81%. The office segment saw the sharpest movement, decreasing by six-basis points to 7.23%. Retail properties followed with a five-basis point decline, bringing their average to 6.84%. Industrial cap rates held relatively steady at 6.39%, a two-basis point increase from the prior quarter.4

blocks.html: In the first half of 2026, we officially launched Blue Owl Digital Infrastructure Fund IV (“BODI IV”). BODI IV builds on our established foundation with a clear focus: continuing to scale with the cloud, approaching AI opportunities with discipline, maintaining underwriting rigor, and investing in differentiation through our power strategy, site selection, community engagement, and adaptive design, all of which we believe position us as a partner of choice for next- generation AI and cloud infrastructure.

blocks.html: Opportunities across sectors remain strong for Blue Owl's Net Lease strategies. Despite ongoing market volatility and global macro pressures, we are seeing heightened demand from companies seeking strategic capital. This trend has expanded the universe of attractive opportunities, fueling a growing pipeline. As a result, we are building a higher-quality roster of potential credit tenants at increasingly favorable pricing.

blocks.html: Fund Overview | Q1 2026

On March 29, 2024, we held the final close for Blue Owl Real Estate Fund VI (the “Fund” or “Fund VI”) for a total of $5.2 billion in capital commitments. Since holding our first close in December 2022, we have acquired $8.0 billion in gross assets, totaling 27 investments across 525 properties. We have a strong pipeline of attractive potential transactions and remain focused on delivering strong risk-adjusted returns to our investors.

• STORE concluded Q1 2026 with 3,577 individual property investments and $17.3 billion in AUM
• The company’s portfolio demonstrates strong fund-level metrics as of Q1 2026, including a 14.8-year
WALT and 2.1% weighted average annual rent bumps
• Owing to its strong portfolio composition, STORE generated Q1 2026 revenues of $342 million and net
income of $72 million
• Substantially all of STORE Capital’s leases with tenants are structured as triple-net – insulating STORE
Capital from deteriorating economics due to inflationary pressures on insurance, R&M or payroll at the
property level
• STORE Capital maintains its investment grade credit ratings of BBB- (positive outlook) / Baa3 (positive
outlook) / BBB (stable outlook) from S&P, Moody’s, and Fitch

• Intel Corporation once again exceeded quarterly expectations across revenue, gross margin, and EPS,
marking its sixth consecutive quarter of beating financial guidance amid strong demand and disciplined
execution to expand available supply
• In Q1 2026, Intel reported revenue of $13.6 billion and delivered non-GAAP EPS of $0.29, while non-
GAAP net income attributable to Intel rose 156.0% YoY to $1.5 billion. The company initiated strong Q2
guidance and signaled a stronger full-year trajectory
• The company's Data Center and AI segment continues to be a standout performer, generating $5.1
billion in revenue during the quarter—a 22.0% increase YoY—underscoring Intel's expanding role in AI-
driven infrastructure
• The Company announced new strategic initiatives during the quarter to build on the Company’s strength
serving hyperscalers and other data center users. Notably, the Company announced a multi-year
collaboration with Google for continued deployment of Intel’s Xeon processors and for the co-
development of custom ASIC infrastructure processing units

• During Q1 2026, Arko reported revenue of $1.8 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $51 million, an increase
of 65.1% YoY, driven by strong execution across retail, wholesale and fleet fueling segments
• Q1 2026 retail fuel margin increased to 48.0 cents per gallon (up from 38.7 cents per gallon in Q1 2025),
while merchandise margin expanded 70 basis points to 33.9%
• Arko converted 41 retail stores to dealer locations during Q1 2026, bringing total conversions since
program inception in 2024 to 450 sites; the company continues to expect cumulative annualized
operating income benefits of more than $20 million, plus $10 million in structural G&A savings once fully
scaled
• Arko maintains substantial liquidity of ~$1.1 billion, including $272 million in cash on hand and $794
million of remaining availability on the company’s credit lines (Q1 2026). The company is guiding to a full
year adjusted EBITDA of $245-$265mm, versus $248mm in 2025

• On February 24, 2025, SanDisk successfully completed its separation from Western Digital, becoming an
independent public company and trading on the Nasdaq exchange under the ticker ‘SNDK.’ The
separation of the businesses will allow the company to capitalize on unique growth opportunities within
the NAND industry and operate more efficiently with a distinct capital structure
• David Goeckeler assumed the role of Chief Executive Officer of SanDisk after previously serving in the
same role at Western Digital
• For Q1 2026, the company generated total revenues of $6.0 billion (up 97% sequentially) and operating
income of $4.2 billion. Looking ahead, we expect SanDisk to continue benefitting from sustained
investment tied to AI-driven data center build-outs, which is supporting robust demand for memory and
storage solutions
• SanDisk achieved a zero-debt balance sheet as of April 2026, having repaid $1.9 billion in total debt
during the nine months ended April 3, 2026; cash and cash equivalents were $3.7 billion, with nine-month
free cash flow of $4.4 billion
• In late 2025, Moody’s upgraded Sandisk to Ba2 and in early 2026 S&P upgraded the company to BB+.
Both agencies sited favorable demand outlook, favorable pricing dynamics and leverage reduction

rows:
• In Q1 2026, Atlantic Union delivered strong profitability and operating momentum as the Sandy Spring
integration finalized
• Net interest income of $312.4m and pre-provision, pre-tax earnings (FTE) of $161.9m supporting
attractive returns on capital. Both metrics down slightly QoQ as driven by lower day count in the quarter
and decrease in interest income. In addition non-performing assets ticked down 15% in the quarter
• Balance sheet quality remained a highlight with annualized net charge-offs of 0.02% and robust capital
levels (CET1 10.21%; Tier 1 leverage 9.31%), providing capacity to support loan growth across core Mid-
Atlantic markets
• Funding mix continued to improve with lower reliance on higher-cost brokered deposits and stable
customer deposit trends, while management reiterated 2026 targets for adjusted operating ROA,
ROTCE, and efficiency

• In Q1 2026, Syngenta reported $6.4 billion in revenue and $1.4 billion in EBITDA, reflecting an 5%
increase year-over-year. EBITDA margin improved by ~0.6% to 21.9% driven by a higher-margin
business portfolio focus, disciplined cost management, and continued operational efficiency gains
• Corp protection sales were $3.5 billion, up 3% year over year driven by strong growth in Europe and
China. Specifically, Rregional performance included 18% growth in Europe, driven by biologicals, and
nearly 350 product approvals in Q1 2026
• The company continues to invest in R&D, with Syngenta stating continued investment in innovation and
operational efficiency initiatives aimed at improving EBITDA margins and controlling capital expenditures
• Management has indicated the group focused on achieving 20% EBITDA margins by end of 2026
(versus 15.4% in 2025)
• The company maintains investment grade credit ratings from all three major ratings agencies – Baa3 per
Moody’s and BBB per S&P and Fitch

• Bank of the Sierra reported record quarterly net income of $12.5 million in Q1 2026, representing a
47.0% increase over Q4 2025, driven by higher net interest income and lower credit loss exposure
• Net interest margin was 3.75% for Q1 2026; return on average assets (ROAA) was 1.39% and return on
average equity (ROAE) was 13.88% - all metrics exceeded prior year’s quarter
• Total deposits reached $3.0 billion at quarter-end, up 3% YoY, with noninterest-bearing deposits
representing 35% of the total deposit mix; cost of funds declined to 1.33% from 1.46% in Q1 2025
• Notably, non-performing assets decreased to $10 million, which marked a 30% sequential decrease QoQ
as the Company prioritizes balance sheet health
• Shortly after reporting quarterly financials, Bank of the Sierra earned an Outstanding CRA rating from the
FDIC, reflecting the strength of its community reinvestment practices and commitment to the
communities it serves

• Gallup reported FY 2025 revenue of $331 million, a 2.4% decline YoY, with an EBITDA margin from
operations of 18.7% - the company maintained a 73.9% gross margin, reflecting continued operational
discipline
• 2025 EBITDA from operations increased 4.9% from 2024 levels and the company generated $47mm in
FCF for the quarter
• Gallup's balance sheet shows $36 million in cash / investments and a 4.1% increase in total debt to
$44.3mm. The company maintains near full availability on its $100m revolver
• Contract assets increased 45.6% YoY, reflecting strong forward visibility in long-term client engagements
- contract liabilities grew 14.1% YoY, indicating robust advance client commitments and backlog
• Strategic cost management continued with a 13.1% reduction in business development and marketing
expenses, a 9.2% decline in pooled costs, and a 6.8% reduction in total production costs

• For Q2 2026, CommonSpirit reported normalized operating revenues of $10.5 billion, reflecting a $403
million, or 4.0%, increase over the prior year period, driven by strong volume growth and higher provider
fee revenue across its network
• Normalized EBITDA for the quarter reached $550 million, representing an 66% increase compared to
$330 million in the same period of the prior year. Normalized EBITDA removes the one time $352mm
FEMA emergency grant that CommonSpirit received in Q2 2025
• CommonSpirit's volume trajectory remained robust, with adjusted admissions increasing 3.8% year-over-
year, led by particularly strong growth in the Central region (22.4%), Mountain region (12.9%), and
Northwest region (8.3%), while labor productivity continued to improve as salaries and benefits per
adjusted admission declined 1.2% and FTEs per adjusted admission decreased 0.2%
• CommonSpirit maintains healthy liquidity with approximately $17.7 billion of unrestricted cash and
investments

• US Foods reported Q1 2026 results, producing $9.6 billion (+2.8% YoY) and $413 million (+6.2% YoY) in
revenue and adjusted EBITDA, respectively. Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 14 basis points YoY to
4.3%, while adjusted diluted EPS grew 14.7% to $0.78
• Independent restaurant case volume accelerated to +4.6% YoY (organic +4.4%), with healthcare and
hospitality volumes up 3.7% and 5.0%, respectively. Total case volume grew 1.4% (organic +1.1%)
despite a 2.3% decline in chain volume
• Net leverage declined to 2.6x (from 2.7x at year-end FY 2025), within the company's target range of 2.0x
to 3.0x
• US Foods reaffirmed its fiscal year 2026 guidance and expects adjusted EBITDA growth of 9% - 13%
• In December 2025 Moody’s upgraded US Foods’ corporate family rating to Ba1. S&P’s corporate credit
rating remains at BB+. The company maintains its investment grade BBB- secured rating

• During Q1 2026, Fulton Bank generated net interest income of $262 million, achieving a net interest
margin of 3.58%, while the total cost of deposits declined 8 basis points quarter-over-quarter to 1.78%
• Capital ratios remained strong as of March 31, 2026, with CET1 of 11.9%, Tier 1 risk-based of 12.7%,
and a total risk-based capital ratio of 15.1% (all essentially flat from prior quarter)
• Deposits totaled $26.8 billion, a $178.9 million increase compared to $26.6 billion as of December 31,
2025
• Non-interest income remained flat versus prior quarter and continues to be a meaningful contributor at
over 21% of total revenue. This is supported by wealth management AUM/AUA in excess of $17 billion
and diversified commercial and consumer fee income streams
• Fulton Bank continues to make significant technological investments including a new commercial
origination system, new mortgage origination system, new mortgage loan servicing system, new
consumer origination system, and new customer relationship management system to drive growth while
increasing efficiency

• Dollar General generated net sales of $10.9 billion during Q4 2025, a 5.9% YoY increase compared to
$10.3 billion in Q4 2024
• Same-store sales increased 4.3% during the quarter, reflecting a 2.6% increase in customer traffic and a
1.7% increase in average transaction amount. Same-store sales in Q4 2025 included growth in each of
the consumables, seasonal, home products, and apparel categories
• Gross margin in the quarter expanded to 30.4% from 29.4% YoY. The margin expansion was driven by
lower shrink, higher inventory markups and lower inventory damages
• Since its downgrade to Baa3 in March 2025, the company has improved credit metrics across the board,
driven by recovering sales trends, margin expansion, and deleveraging
• Alongside Q4 2025 results, the company also announced plans to open approximately 450 new stores
and remodel 4,000 stores in FY 2026, sustaining its footprint expansion strategy
• The company expects FY 2026 net sales growth to be 3.7% to 4.2% and SSSG to be 2.2% to 2.7%

• Sysco delivered revenues of $20.5 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $970 million for the quarter ended
March 2026, up 4.7% and flat year over year, respectively
• In March 2026, Sysco announced a ~$29.1 billion acquisition of Jetro Restaurant Depot, adding a higher-
margin cash-and-carry platform with 166 warehouses across 35 states and 725,000+ independent
foodservice customers
• The transaction is expected to close by Q3 FY2027, be mid-to-high single digit EPS accretive in year
one, and deliver ~$250 million of annualized net cost synergies within three years
• Sysco is expected to fund the acquisition with $21bn of new and hybrid debt. As a result, Moody’s and
S&P put the company on review for downgrade / negative outlook
• Gross profit grew 6.5% year over year to $3.8 billion, driven by positive volumes, strategic sourcing
efficiencies, and effective management of product cost inflation
• Sysco holds an investment grade rating of BBB / Baa2 / BBB from S&P/Moody’s/Fitch

• Since acquiring TravelCenters of America in May 2023, BP has continually expanded its nationwide site
network and explored new store opportunities, accelerating expansion and integration efforts across
convenience, EV charging, and biofuels to support its U.S. growth strategy
• During Q1 2026, BP generated revenue of $52.3 billion (up 11.5% YoY) and underlying replacement cost
profit of $3.2 billion, more than doubling from $1.4 billion in Q1 2025, driven by strong oil trading, higher
refining margins and resilient upstream production of 2.3 million barrels of oil equivalent per day
• Q1 2026 operating cash flow was $2.9 billion, reflecting a $6.0 billion adjusted working capital build
driven by the rising price environment and seasonal inventory builds
• BP reiterated its 2026 capital expenditure guidance of $13.0 billion to $13.5 billion, but expects
production to be lower due to Middle East Disruption
• Net debt increased to $25.3 billion as of March 2026, up from $22.2 billion at year-end 2025, primarily
driven by the $6.0 billion working capital build; the company maintains a target of $14.0 billion to $18.0
billion of net debt by the end of 2027
• BP agreed to divest the Gelsenkirchen refinery in Q1 2026, further supporting its structural cost reduction
program; the company raised its cost-reduction target to $6.5 billion to $7.5 billion by 2027, up from
cumulative reductions of $2.8 billion delivered through 2025

• On March 5, 2025, Walgreens Boots Alliance announced an agreement with Sycamore Partners that
would take the company private at an enterprise value of up to $23.7 billion
• Based on public reporting, we believe that Sycamore’s investment strategy is aligned with the turnaround
strategy enacted by existing management – this strategy refocuses Walgreens around the US Retail
Pharmacy Segment (i.e.Blue Owl’s tenant)
• The take private closed in August 2025 in line with expected business plan
• The Company remains compliant with all leases and based on conversations with Walgreens Real Estate
leadership – Blue Owl’s portfolio is well positioned for the future

• CoreWeave generated $2.1 billion of revenue in Q1 2026, up 112% year over year and 32% sequentially,
bringing the company to a record quarterly result
• Adjusted EBITDA totaled $1.2 billion in Q1 2026, representing a 56% margin and 91% year-over-year
growth
• Revenue backlog grew to $99.4 billion as of March 31, 2026, supporting multi-year revenue visibility
• CoreWeave surpassed 1 GW of active power in Q1 2026 while expanding total contracted power to more
than 3.5 GW
• The company secured more than $20 billion of debt and equity capital year-to-date, headlined by an $8.5
billion investment-grade-rated (A- equivalent) non-recourse term loan and a $2 billion equity investment
from NVIDIA; S&P moved CoreWeave's corporate rating outlook from Stable to Positive
• CoreWeave continues to diversify its customer base with additional customer and partner momentum in
Q1 2026 included landmark new commitments from Anthropic and Meta (a $21 billion agreement), a $6
billion capacity expansion with Jane Street, and new wins with Hudson River Trading, World Labs, and
Physics X

• Commercial momentum accelerated with $227m of new wins and a record $2.7bn sales pipeline, with notable

• Financial flexibility remained a strength with $1.6bn of total liquidity at quarter-end and net leverage of ~2.5x,

• As of Q1 2026, Old National Bank demonstrated a robust balance sheet with $73.0 billion of total assets, $39
billion of AUM and $55.7 billion of total deposits, up 4.2% annualized from Q4 2025
• Net charge-offs were $32.0 million, or 26 bps of average loans, compared to 27 bps in prior quarter
• Old National maintained a healthy 11.6% Tier 1 capital ratio and 8.9% leverage ratio as of March 31, 2026,
with tangible book value per share of $13.93, up 11.0% year-over-year
• Old National Bancorp currently maintains an investment-grade (Baa1) credit rating from Moody’s

• Starbucks generated $9.5 billion of consolidated net revenue during Q2 FY2026 (+9% YoY) and comparable
sales growth of highlighting the continued success of the "Back to Starbucks" turnaround plan
• Global comparable store sales increased 6.2% during the quarter, with North America comparable store sales
accelerating to 7.1%
• International segment revenue advanced 10% YoY, while international operating margin expanded to 19.4%
• Starbucks completed the sale of a 60% stake in its China retail operations to Boyu Capital shortly after quarter-
end, receiving approximately $3.1 billion in gross cash proceeds with total transaction value to Starbucks
expected to exceed $13 billion; proceeds have been and will continue to be deployed toward debt reduction
consistent with the company's BBB+ / Baa1 credit profile
• For the balance of the year – the company expects continued momentum with Global and U.S. comparable
store sales growth of 5.0% or greater

• Oracle reported remaining performance obligations of $553 billion as of the fiscal quarter ended February 28,
2026 – up 325% YoY owing to the rapid growth in demand for AI training and cloud computing services
globally
• The growth in Oracle’s backlog has translated into robust revenue growth. The company reported $17.2 billion
in revenues over the quarter ended February 28, 2026, representing YoY growth of 22% (18% in constant
currency)
• Profitability has remained strong year-to-date, with the company generating $5.2 billion in Non-GAAP net
income over the most recent quarter, a 23% YoY growth rate (18% in constant currency)
• In February, Oracle announced a $50 billion dollar capital raise in debt and equity financing. In addition, the
company does not expect to issue any additional bonds beyond this amount in calendar year 2026
• On April 16, 2026, Oracle announced an expanded multicloud partnership with Amazon Web Services. This
represents the latest addition to Oracle's interconnect partnerships, which now span 26 partner cloud regions

• During Q1 2026, SouthState Bank generated net interest income of $562 million, up 3% year over year,
achieving a net interest margin of 3.8%
• Loans increased 7% annualized in Q1 2026, supported by a 50% increase in loan pipelines since last summer
and more than a doubling of loan production in Texas and Colorado to $1.1 billion; deposits grew 5%
annualized with an ending loan-to-deposit ratio of 89%
• The company delivered 1.37% return on average assets (up from 0.56% in Q1 2025, but down 10bps
sequentially)
• Asset quality remains strong, with annualized net charge-offs of just 9 basis points in Q1 2026 and total
allowance for credit losses plus reserve for unfunded commitments of 1.32% of loans
• SouthState Bank remains the fifth largest bank in the southern United States, and maintains an investment-
grade issuer rating of Baa3 from Moody's and a strong A- rating from the Kroll Bond Rating Agency

rows:
• Alphabet continues to demonstrate meaningful growth - generating $109.9 billion of revenue and $46.4
billion of EBITDA in Q1 2026, with year-over-year growth of 21.8% and 31.6%, respectively, reflecting
sustained momentum across core businesses
• Alphabet’s proprietary TPU infrastructure continues to drive strong demand, with Anthropic expanding its
Google Cloud relationship to access up to 1 million TPUs, representing tens of billions of dollars of AI
compute capacity and well over 1 GW coming online in 2026 to train and serve next-generation Claude
models
• Google Cloud delivered robust performance in Q1 2026, with revenues increasing 63.4% year over year
to $20.0 billion, supported by rising enterprise adoption of Google Cloud Platform across AI
infrastructure, enterprise AI solutions, and core GCP offerings
• The company is exceptionally well capitalized with $127 billion of cash and short term investments on
balance sheet and negative net leverage, driving ratings of AA+ / Aa2 / AA+ (S&P / Moody’s / Fitch)

• ReSRG Automotive is a newly-formed, Tier 1 auto-manufacturing company serving investment-grade,
blue-chip auto OEMs including Mercedes-Benz, Toyota, Volkswagen, GM and BMW
• The company was founded upon the merger of REHAU Automotive and SRG Global, two companies that
were merged under the management of Atlas Holdings, a financial sponsor with more than $16 billion in
AUM and deep experience in the automotive manufacturing segment
• In Q1 2026, the company generated $575mm in revenue and $33m in Adjusted EBITDA (5.7% margin),
demonstrating a meaningful sequential step-up from Q4 2025
• In April 2026, ReSRG Automotive expanded its strategic partnership with Valeo, a world leader in
automotive lighting systems, broadening the scope of collaboration from illuminated front panels to a full
range of plastic-based illuminated exterior components while simultaneously extending the geographic
reach of the alliance to include China alongside the existing Europe and North America footprint
• Company maintains IG ratings, BBB and BBB-, from both KBRA and Egan-Jones respectively on the
basis of its low net leverage (0.6x), ample scale ($1.9 billion in fiscal year 2025 revenues) and
exceptional financial visibility (96% of forecasted FY 2026 revenues have been fully contracted already)

• During Q1 2026, Amerant delivered $80.3 million in net interest income, down nearly 6.5% YoY, primarily
reflecting the impact of the repricing of the loan portfolio following rate cuts. Amerant reported noninterest
income of $17.4 million, down 11% from prior year due to a Q1 2025 non-recurring gain from sale
• Amerant Bank maintained a strong balance sheet, closing the year with $9.9 billion in total assets
• Amerant maintains robust capital levels, with tangible common equity representing 9.0% of tangible
assets and a Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) ratio of 11.4% (up 4bps from Q4 2025), a key regulatory
measure of common equity relative to risk-weighted assets
• Net interest margin contracted slightly during the quarter to 3.55% in Q1 2026, reflecting the full-quarter
impact of 50-bps of rate cuts during Q4 2025. While down slightly, Amerant’s net interest margin remains
healthy

• Eaton delivered record Q1 2026 results with sales of $7.5 billion, up 17% YoY, consisting of 10% organic
growth, 4% from acquisitions, and 3% from favorable foreign exchange
• Eaton’s backlog continues to expand and currently sits at $14.5bn driven by 48% growth in the Electrical
sector and 28% growth in Aerospace sector
• The company closed two strategic acquisitions during the quarter, totaling $11bn — Boyd Thermal,
positioning Eaton as a "grid-to-chip" provider of liquid cooling infrastructure for data centers (revenue up
well over 100% YoY with backlog doubled in six months), and Ultra PCS, expanding its presence in
defense aerospace
• Q1 free cash flow increased 245% YoY, and management raised its full year guidance, now expecting 9-
11% organic growth (up from a midpoint of 8% organic growth)
